question: A 30-year-old man presents after high-speed road-traffic trauma with suspected pelvic fracture. Which is the most appropriate first-line imaging?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Ultrasound is excellent for fluid detection (FAST) but cannot adequately assess cortical bone detail for fracture characterisation.
MRI provides excellent soft tissue and bone-marrow detail but is too time-consuming and logistically difficult in acute major trauma.
Correct. An AP pelvic radiograph is the rapid, widely available first-line investigation for suspected pelvic fracture in trauma, guiding the need for subsequent CT.
Bone scintigraphy detects subtle or occult fractures but is far too slow for acute trauma assessment.

overallFeedback.feedback: Not quite. In acute trauma, plain radiography is the rapid first-line tool; CT follows for fracture characterisation or haemodynamically unstable patients.
Correct! Plain X-ray (AP pelvis) is the standard first-line modality in acute pelvic trauma — fast, available, and diagnostic for most significant fractures.
